name: Federated States of Micronesia
summary: Four island states (Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae) across the western Pacific, ruled by Spain, Germany, Japan and the US; independent in free association with the US since 1986.

knownFor.label: Nan Madol
knownFor.note: Stone city built on reefs (from about 1180).

location.value: Western Pacific; combined land area of about 702 km² across four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei and Kosrae.
location.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

terrain.value: Over 600 islands: high volcanic islands such as Pohnpei and Kosrae, the islands of Chuuk Lagoon and Yap, and many low coral atolls.

climate.value: Hot, humid tropical climate with heavy rain; Pohnpei is among the wettest places on Earth, and typhoons strike Yap and Chuuk.

resources.value: Tuna in a huge ocean zone, earning fishing licence fees, plus coconuts, breadfruit, taro and black pepper grown on Pohnpei.

disasters.value: Cyclones, droughts and rising sea levels.

population.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

urbanisation.value: Mostly villages; the capital Palikir is on Pohnpei near Kolonia, the largest town, and Weno is the main town of Chuuk.

disease.value: Diabetes and heart disease from imported food.

migration.value: Many citizens move to Guam, Hawaii and the US mainland, which they can enter freely to live and work under the Compact.

economicBase.value: Mainly subsistence farming and fishing, with US financial assistance the primary source of revenue.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

tradeRoutes.value: Shipping and United Airlines “island hopper” flights link Pohnpei, Chuuk, Kosrae and Yap with Guam and Hawaii.

wealth.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

moneyAndTax.value: Uses the US dollar; income comes mainly from Compact grants and fishing fees, plus import and income taxes.

inequality.value: Gap between the capital and outer islands.

governmentType.value: A federal republic with a unicameral Congress of fourteen members and no formal political parties; in free association with the United States, which handles defence (Compact renewed in 2004).
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

keyRulers.value: Congress elects the president and vice president from among its four state senators. Tosiwo Nakayama is not named in the part read.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

succession.value: Congress elects the president and vice-president from among its four-year senators; by custom the post rotates among the states.

institutions.value: A one-chamber Congress of 14 senators (one at-large senator from each state, ten by population), state governments and a Supreme Court.

stability.value: Politically stable since independence, with peaceful elections, though the states compete over shares of US funding.

eliteConflict.value: Chuuk State set up a commission to study leaving the federation, and a vote planned for 2015 was postponed indefinitely.

armyAndTech.value: No army: the United States handles defence under the Compact, and many citizens serve in the US armed forces; police patrol the seas.

majorWars.value: In February 1944 the US Navy launched Operation Hailstone, a massive attack on Truk Lagoon. The part read does not cover wars since independence.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: No changes since 1986; Palau and the Marshall Islands chose separate paths out of the US Trust Territory in the late 1970s.

alliancesRivals.value: Compact of Free Association with the United States (since 1986), which gives US defence and aid.

inventions.value: Traditional navigation by stars and swells.

scienceEducation.value: University of the South Pacific campuses.

openness.value: Open to visitors and trade but heavily dependent on imported food, fuel and goods.

communicationTransport.value: Boats and field-trip ships to the outer islands, United Airlines island-hopper flights, and an undersea internet cable to Pohnpei.

religion.value: 95.3% Christian in 2016 (52.6% Roman Catholic, 41.7% Protestant); the body text gives about 97%.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: English; Chuukese, Pohnpeian, Yapese, Kosraean and others.

artsArchitecture.value: The basalt ruins of Nan Madol on Pohnpei (a World Heritage Site), Yapese stone money (rai) and men’s houses, and woven mats.

socialStructure.value: Matrilineal clans and chiefly titles in each state, such as the nahnmwarki paramount chiefs of Pohnpei and Yap’s ranked villages.

sharedIdentity.value: People identify first with their island and state; a national identity is still developing alongside a wider Pacific identity.

dailyLife.value: Breadfruit, taro, yams, fish and coconut, with growing use of imported rice and tinned food; sakau (kava) is drunk on Pohnpei.

neighbours.value: Palau to the west, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands to the north, the Marshall Islands to the east and Papua New Guinea to the south.

ideasReligions.value: Christianity combined with customary chiefly systems, plus strong concern about climate change and rising seas.

colonisation.value: Germany acquired the islands from Spain in 1899 and held them until 1914; Japan captured them in the First World War and held a League of Nations mandate; the US administered them from 1947 to 1994.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

riseSignals.value: Constitution adopted in 1979; the Compact of Free Association with the US took effect in 1986, ending most of the UN trusteeship.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge. The page says the Compact of Free Association was renewed in 2004; the 2023 renewal is not mentioned.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: The Compact of Free Association entered into force on 3 November 1986, ending the trusteeship.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Federated States of Micronesia (checked 13 Nov 2026)

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
